metadata.title: Isaiah Likely hauls in touchdown Sunday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants 34-27 loss against the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Likely continued his success at finding the end zone. He nearly caught a second one as J.J. McCarthy just missed looking to find him to tie the game at the end of the game. He remains a locked in TE1.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Another big day in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Likely caught six of 11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints.
metadata.analysis: The tight end came through with another big performance and connected with J.J. McCarthy on a 24-yard TD in the fourth quarter after the young QB had replaced Jameis Winston under center. It's reassuring that Likely remained involved even after the switch at quarterback, and he's seen double-digit targets in three straight games, delivering a 24-259-3 line on 36 targets as the team's No. 2 pass catcher behind Malik Nabers. Likely will look to keep rolling in Week 7 against the Texans, regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely's Breakout in Full Swing After Another Big Game in Week 6
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely is certainly enjoying his first season in the Big Apple in 2026. Likely was a big contributor once again in Sunday's Week 6 loss to the visiting New Orleans Saints, catching six of his 11 targets for 99 yards and one touchdown. The 26-year-old's 11 targets were second to receiver Malik Nabers' 15, and his 99 yards trailed only Nabers as well. The big game came in a contest in which veteran quarterback Jameis Winston was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy. Likely's production did not slow after the switch under center, and his touchdown catch came on a 24-yard hookup with McCarthy in the fourth quarter as the Giants tried to make things interesting in an eventual 34-27 loss. He has been the clear No. 2 target behind Nabers in what has been a pass-happy offense under head coach John Harbaugh. Likely is coming through on his breakout potential in New York, as he is currently the No. 1 overall in half-PPR scoring with 39 catches, 383 yards, and five touchdowns in his first six games played. He should be locked into all starting fantasy lineups for his Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans.

metadata.title: Fire Up Isaiah Likely as a TE1 Against Saints
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely had a monster game in Week 5, hauling in 11 of 13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdowns in the 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders. After a sluggish start with Jameis Winston taking over as the starter, Likely has snapped off two very productive weeks in a row, totaling 160 yards and two touchdowns on 18 receptions. The former Ravens tight end has emerged as one of the best in the NFL, averaging 13.8 half-PPR fantasy points per game, and is currently the TE2, trailing only Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. He faces a New Orleans Saints defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season and has struggled mightily in recent weeks. In what projects to be a high-scoring affair, fantasy managers can fire up Likely as a TE1 in Week 6.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Rising After Massive Day Against Commanders
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely (foot) recorded a career-high 11 receptions on 13 targets (tying a career-high) in a 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders in Week 5. He posted 94 yards and two touchdowns against the Commanders as well. Likely is dealing with a foot injury, but was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. He enters a Week 6 matchup with the New Orleans Saints as RotoBaller's No. 4 tight end this week. Likely is projected to score 10.6 fantasy points. According to Pro Football Reference, the Saints allow 9.5 fantasy points per game to tight ends. Likely is currently started in 70% of Yahoo leagues, but that number will almost certainly increase for Week 6. He is a must-start player moving forward.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely (foot) practicing in full for Week 6
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Likely remains a strong TE1 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely hauls in two touchdowns in Week 5 tie with Commanders
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely hauled in 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants' 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Likely has made the most of his involvement in the New York passing attack to this point, recording over 65 receiving yards in three of the first five games. The tight end remains one of the more impactful options in the Giants offense early on for new head coach John Harbaugh ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Two TDs among career-high 11 catches
metadata.description: Likely caught 11 of 13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Likely's career-high 11 receptions included a three-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter and a 17-yard touchdown reception in the fourth, which helped the Giants erase a 19-6 second-half deficit. The shifty TE has drawn double-digit targets in three of his first five games with the Giants, producing 33 catches for 284 yards and four TDs. Likely needs 193 receiving yards to match his 2024 regular-season career high from the third of his four seasons in Baltimore. He and Malik Nabers should continue to work as the Giants' top two pass catchers in Week 6 against the Saints.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Remains a TE1 Option in Week 5
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely (groin) is off the injury report and expected to play against the division-rival Washington Commanders. After being limited on Wednesday and Thursday with a groin issue, Likely completed a full practice on Friday and is ready to go in Week 5. After back-to-back down games in Weeks 2 and 3, Likely bounced back, hauling in seven of 12 targets for 66 yards in the 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals. While he hasn't lived up to expectations since his Week 1 breakout, Likely remains a reliable option at tight end. He faces a Commanders defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points to tight ends this season and has already seen Dallas Goedert and Jake Ferguson post monster games. While rain and wind could be a factor, Likely is a low-end TE1 in Week 5.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Likely hauled in seven passes last week. He remains a borderline TE1/TE2 play for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Good to go for Week 5
metadata.description: Likely (knee/groin) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game at Washington, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: With limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Likely was upgraded to full Friday and is all systems go for Sunday's divisional matchup. He's coming off a season-high 12 targets in last Sunday's win over the Cardinals and has 22 catches for 190 yards and two touchdowns on 35 targets through four games as a TE1 in fantasy.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Another limited practice
metadata.description: Likely (knee/groin) practiced on a limited basis Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Likely maintained his activity level from Wednesday's session as he deals with knee and groin injuries. There's been nothing to suggest that he's in danger of missing Sunday's game at Washington, but he still may be tagged with a designation on the Giants' final practice report of the week Friday.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran tight end was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday as he continues to recover from a pair of injuries. He seems likely to play in Week 5, but we won't know his official status until the team releases their final practice report after Friday's practice.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely was limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Likely is coming off hailing in seven passes last week. He remains a low-end TE1 if he's good to go.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Likely (knee/groin) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Likely is tending to a pair of health concerns as Week 5 prep begins, but he at least has two more chances to get back to full this week and avoid a designation ahead of Sunday's game at Washington. Through four contests this season, he's been a key cog in the Giants' passing game, totaling 22 catches (on 35 targets) for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely hauls in seven passes Sunday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely hauled in 7-of-12 targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: Likely had a nice bounce-back game on Sunday, finishing with seven catches for 66 yards in the team's win over the Cardinals. He could prove to have solid week-to-week fantasy upside with Jameis Winston at the helm for the Giants, but he will likely continue to struggle with consistency moving forward.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Team-high seven grabs in win over Cards
metadata.description: Likely caught seven of 12 targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over Arizona.
metadata.analysis: The targets and catches led the Giants on the day, but Likely's yardage total was well behind Malik Nabers' 112. Likely has remained an important part of the passing game with Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), and in Winston's three appearances (two starts) the tight end has delivered a 14-112-0 line on 27 targets, seeing double-digit looks twice. Likely will look to find the end zone for the first time since the season opener in a Week 5 road clash with the Commanders.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Looking to Bounce Back Against Cardinals
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely is looking to bounce back after a down game in Week 3. He caught just two of five targets for 13 yards in the 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans. In two games with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, Likely has caught just seven of 15 targets for 46 yards, averaging just 4.1 half-PPR fantasy points per game. On a positive note, Likely's usage has improved significantly from his Week 1 role, with 77% of snaps and 85% of routes over the last two weeks. He also faces an Arizona Cardinals defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season, including a monster performance against 49ers star tight end George Kittle in Week 3. While his struggles with Winston could pose a threat to his Week 4 outlook, Likely should be considered a low-end TE1 against a weaker Cardinals secondary.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Takes a Big Step Backward with Quarterback Downgrade
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has cooled back down following a scorching hot start to the season. Likely made his Giants debut in Week 1 with an impressive stat line of eight catches, 78 yards, and two touchdowns, but his fantasy production has declined in every game since then. His reduced productivity is a direct result of the Giants losing quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) for the season. New York has been forced to start Jameis Winston, and the veteran hasn't been able to match Dart's prowess in the passing attack. For a large portion of his career, Winston was viewed as a quarterback who could support top-end wide receiver and tight end production because he loved to air the football out. He's still pass-happy, but as of late, he has been delivering more turnovers and fewer completions than we'd like to see. As a result, Likely has fallen outside the top 12 tight ends in fantasy football as long as Winston is under center.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Only two catches vs. Tennessee
metadata.description: Likely caught two of five targets for 13 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: After logging 13 catches through the first two games of the regular season, Likely was held to only two receptions in Week 3, the first game with Jameis Winston as the starter instead of Jaxson Dart (knee, IR). Likely's five targets were second-most on the Giants behind Malik Nabers (six), but the scoring floors of all Giants pass catchers figure to be lower with Winston under center. That said, New York could turn the keys over to the recently acquired J.J. McCarthy if Winston continues to underwhelm. The Giants will stay home for Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense gave up a 6-82-2 receiving line to tight end George Kittle in a 36-30 loss to the 49ers in Week 3.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely quiet in win Sunday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-5 targets for just 13 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wasn't able to get much going on Sunday, finishing with just 13 yards in the team's narrow win over the Titans. He isn't likely to return to fantasy relevance for however long QB Jameis Winston is starting for New York, however, so fantasy managers shouldn't have any hesitations to drop him at this point.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely a Low-End TE1 With Rough Conditions Expected in Week 3
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has been highly productive in his first few weeks with his new team. Through two games, Likely has hauled in 13 of 18 targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 14.8 half-PPR fantasy points per game. Despite wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) being healthy and active to start the season, Likely has been the team's lead receiver in every statistical category. However, quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) underwent season-ending surgery, and backup Jameis Winston will take over as starter. With Dart out, this Matt Nagy offense could lean more on the run game as it tries to limit Winston's turnovers. They face a Tennessee Titans defense that has allowed just 35 yards to tight ends in two games this season, but the main concern is the weather, with heavy rain and winds expected in East Rutherford on Sunday. While it's difficult to take Likely out of starting lineups given his consistent production, fantasy managers should temper expectations in Week 3.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely hauls in five passes Monday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely hauled in 5-of-10 targets for 33 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: Likely didn't put up great numbers on Monday night, finishing with just 33 yards in a loss to the Rams. He was still the most targeted player on the team by far, however, which is a good sign that he will bounce back and return to form sometime in the near future. His bounce back may be delayed is Jaxson Dart (knee) has to miss time for the Giants.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Solid despite Dart injury
metadata.description: Likely secured five of 10 targets for 33 yards in the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Likely's first catch came on one of Jaxson Dart's three completions before he exited the game with a knee injury, and the veteran tight end remained an integral component of the air attack once Jameis Winston took over. Likely's reception and target totals were team-high figures, and he's quickly generated a 13-111-2 line on 18 targets over his first two games in a Giants uniform heading into a Week 3 home matchup against the Titans on Sunday.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Leads Team in Targets Against Rams
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely hauled in five of 10 targets for 33 yards in the 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Despite lackluster fantasy production, Likely led all receivers with 10 targets and played 69% of snaps, a significant increase from Week 1. However, starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) went down on the team's opening drive, and backup Jameis Winston struggled in relief. Winston completed 40% of his passes for 111 yards with no touchdowns. If Dart is forced to miss time with his knee injury, Likely, along with the rest of the Giants' playmakers, would be negatively affected if Winston is unable to produce. While he's still a mid-TE1, fantasy managers should be patient with the former Ravens tight end.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Aims To Follow Up On Great Debut in Week 2
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely delivered a sensational Week 1 performance against the Dallas Cowboys. In his first game with the Giants, Likely hauled in all eight of his targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns, finishing the week as the TE2 in half-PPR formats. The former Raven was a major factor on third downs, hauling in five catches that resulted in first-down conversions. However, he played less than half the snaps in Week 1 (49%) and ran just 68% of the routes. While Jaxson Dart had one of the best games of his career in Week 1, any regression from the second-year quarterback would likely impact Likely, given his limited snaps and route participation. He faces a Los Angeles Rams defense that allowed the eighth-fewest yards to tight ends in 2025 and held 49ers tight end George Kittle in check in Week 1. While his great game was a positive sign, fantasy managers should still value him as a low-to-mid TE1 in Week 2.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Looks to Build on Fast Start
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely went off on Monday Night Football against the Cowboys, hauling in eight targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns. He led the team in receiving yards while finishing second in targets, just one behind Malik Nabers. Likely showed his athleticism and his scheme fit with new offensive coordinator Matt Nagy designing plays for him similar to the schemes that led to Travis Kelce flourishing under Nagy in Kansas City. He has a tough matchup in Week 2 against the Rams, but he looks ready to live up to the hype and be a true top-10 TE this season in a very heavily involved role with the Giants.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely hauls in two touchdowns in win Sunday
metadata.description: Isaiah Likely caught eight passes for 78 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Likely exceeded expectations in his first game as a Giant on Sunday. He led the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns on the night, scoring twice in what turned out to be a huge win over the Cowboys. His involvement on this offense looks great right now and he will likely be one of the hot waiver additions this week in any league he's not already rostered in.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Shines With Two Touchdowns Against Cowboys
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely hauled in all eight targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. Likely was the team's leading receiver throughout training camp, and he lived up to the hype in Week 1. Of his eight catches, four came on third down. Despite playing only 49% of the snaps in Week 1, he looks primed for a key role in the passing game this season. With quarterback Jaxson Dart and the Giants offense looking sharp in Week 1, Likely should continue to see valuable opportunities in the passing game. He faces the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2, where Likely should be considered a mid-TE1 despite the limited snap share.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely - Scores twice in Week 1 win
metadata.description: Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-20 win over the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Likely showcased excellent chemistry with quarterback Jaxson Dart, as all of their attempted connections resulted in completions, including touchdowns of 15 yards in the second quarter and two yards in the third, which turned a 7-7 tie into a 21-7 Giants lead. Malik Nabers (knee) suited up and led the team with nine targets, but no other teammate exceeded four targets or 27 receiving yards. Likely looks like an integral piece of the Giants' passing game heading into a Week 2 road game against the Rams on Monday Night Football.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely a Strong Starting Option Against Cowboys
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely is set to make his debut in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. Likely signed a three-year, $40 million contract with the Giants this offseason, reuniting with former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh in New York. During his time in Baltimore, he had 135 receptions for 1,568 yards and 15 touchdowns in 63 games as the backup tight end behind Mark Andrews. Likely has been a key part of the Giants' offense throughout training camp, leading the team in receiving with star Malik Nabers (knee) missing most of camp. If Nabers is inactive or has a limited snap count in Week 1, Likely has a legitimate shot to be the team's leading receiver against the Cowboys' defense, which allowed the most passing yards in the NFL last season. Likely profiles as a low-end TE1 in the season opener and should be a solid starting option.

metadata.title: Isaiah Likely Could Hit The Ground Running This Season
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely is creating some real buzz in the fantasy community, mostly because he is no longer blocked from playing time behind Mark Andrews for the Baltimore Ravens. He has been impressive in training camp, and there is a real belief among many who follow the team that he emerges as the No. 2 target behind Malik Nabers on the outside for the Giants. Adam Bernstein of GMENHQ, a Giants blog, wrote this about Likely: "Given the state of New York's receiver room, there's a real chance he functions as Dart's No. 2 receiving option behind Malik Nabers." Likely played in 14 games last year with the Baltimore Ravens and caught 27 passes for 307 yards and a touchdown, playing most of the season behind Andrews on the depth chart. This is an opportunity for a breakout season for Likely in an expanded role.
